Duorem needs local network access to find, wake and control your computer. Choose Allow local network access to grant permission.

Connect to your home Wi-Fi or Ethernet network to discover reachable devices. Duorem first detects MAC addresses with NetBIOS. On rooted devices, optional root lookup can be enabled from the menu. Otherwise, enter the MAC address from the computer or router.

Verify this fingerprint directly on your computer before trusting it. A changed key can indicate a different computer or an intercepted connection.

Duorem controls one computer on your local network. Wake-on-LAN sends a magic packet to turn it on. Shutdown and Restart connect through SSH and run commands on the computer. Wake-on-LAN and SSH are separate features and can be configured independently.
Why discovery may miss a device

The computer must be on and connected to the same IPv4 Wi-Fi or Ethernet network while you search. Android 10 and newer prevent ordinary apps from reading the system ARP table, so Duorem first asks devices for their MAC address using NetBIOS. Not every device supports that. A rooted phone can optionally try the network neighbor table; otherwise enter the wired MAC address manually from the computer or router. Firewalls, large subnets, and slow responses can also hide a device.

The MAC address identifies the network adapter and is required for Wake-on-LAN. The IP address or hostname is used to check status and connect through SSH. The WOL broadcast address is where the magic packet is sent, commonly ending in .255 on a home network. Duorem can usually calculate it from the current network, but unusual network layouts may require manual values.

Green means the device is reachable and SSH is ready. Green with amber text means the device is reachable but SSH is unavailable or not configured. Amber means Duorem is checking. Red means the device is unreachable or the phone has no usable local network. A computer can be online even when it ignores ping; an open configured SSH port also counts as reachable.

Wake-on-LAN must be enabled in the computer firmware, operating system, and network adapter. It is most reliable over wired Ethernet; many computers cannot wake over Wi-Fi. Duorem is designed for the local IPv4 network. Routers normally do not forward broadcast packets from mobile data or the Internet. Sending a packet successfully does not prove that the computer received it or woke up.

The computer needs an SSH server with password authentication and permission to run the configured shutdown command. Duorem defaults to sudo shutdown commands and uses the SSH password for sudo. SSH keys and a separate sudo password are not supported. Before the first command, compare the displayed server fingerprint with the computer and trust it in the app. Duorem never accepts new or changed host keys automatically.

All widgets follow Duorem’s single configured device, even after you edit or replace it. Each widget can have its own label. Background status updates can be turned off or requested every 30 seconds, 1, 5, 10, or 30 minutes, or every 1 or 2 hours. The default is 30 minutes. Android may delay these checks, so the status is not real time. Button taps always perform a fresh check: Power shuts down when SSH is ready, wakes when the device is unreachable, and sends no command when the device is online without SSH. Restart always requires SSH.

Check that the phone is on the correct local network and that local network access is allowed. Verify the wired MAC address, broadcast address, SSH port, username, password, and shutdown command. Check the computer and router firewalls. Try manual configuration if discovery fails. After changing the SSH server, open Duorem and verify its new fingerprint before using a widget.
Configure a device in Duorem before adding a widget.
Add a MAC address for Wake-on-LAN or SSH settings before creating a widget.
All Duorem widgets control this single configured device and follow it when you edit or replace it.
Android may delay background checks to save power, especially at short intervals. Commands always check the current status again.
The Power button shuts down when SSH is ready and sends Wake-on-LAN when the device is unreachable. Restart requires SSH. Every button tap checks the current status before acting.
